boundary: Fictional held-out briefs frozen on 2026-11-12, before the audit-driven skill changes. They state settled jobs, facts and behaviour only; no expected surface, layout, palette, icon style, metaphor or candidate count is encoded.

cases.name: Northbank Physio
cases.brief: Design a complete single-page front-desk workspace for Northbank Physio, a fictional clinic with four physiotherapists. Reception staff keep it open all day to run today's schedule and handle bookings. The job, data and rules are settled; structure, composition, interaction design and visual direction are open. Therapists: Ana Petrov, Daniel Okoye, Mira Lind, Tomas Weber. Today is Tuesday 14 October 2025. Today's appointments: 08:30 Ana Petrov, Lena Fischer, 45 min, knee rehabilitation, arrived; 09:00 Mira Lind, Jonas Berg, 30 min, lower back pain, arrived; 09:15 Daniel Okoye, Sofia Marin, 60 min, shoulder assessment (new patient), arrived; 10:00 Tomas Weber, Aaron Cole, 30 min, ankle sprain follow-up; 10:30 Ana Petrov, Priya Nair, 45 min, hip rehabilitation after surgery; 11:00 Daniel Okoye, Felix Braun, 30 min, neck pain; 11:00 Daniel Okoye, Eva Novak, 30 min, tennis elbow (this double booking is real and staff need to notice it); 13:30 Mira Lind, Henrik Dahl, 60 min, running injury; 14:00 Tomas Weber, Clara Moss, 45 min, plantar fasciitis; 15:30 Ana Petrov, Omar Haddad, 30 min, wrist strain; 16:00 Mira Lind, Nora Quinn, 45 min, postnatal back pain. Patient records: Lena Fischer, +49 30 5550 1123, born 12 March 1984, last visits 30 Sep, 23 Sep and 16 Sep 2025 with Ana Petrov, care note 'Avoid deep knee flexion beyond 90 degrees until review on 28 October'; Sofia Marin, +49 30 5550 4410, born 2 July 1991, no previous visits, care note 'Referral letter from Dr. Hale received'; Felix Braun, +49 30 5550 2087, born 19 November 1976, last visits 7 Oct and 30 Sep 2025 with Daniel Okoye, no care notes. Other patients' records show only name and phone; use fictional numbers in the +49 30 5550 format. Staff must be able to: see today's schedule by therapist; see who has arrived and mark a patient arrived; book an appointment by finding an existing patient or adding a new one (name, phone, reason) and choosing therapist, date, start time and 30, 45 or 60 minutes; reschedule an appointment; cancel an appointment with a reason (patient cancelled, clinic cancelled, no-show); and open a patient's record. A cancellation by the patient less than 24 hours before the start carries a EUR 20 late fee that staff must see before confirming. Behaviour to simulate locally: the week view takes about one second to load; saving a booking succeeds, except that booking Daniel Okoye at 15:00 today fails because the slot was just taken, and staff must be able to recover without losing what they entered. Primary use is a 1440 px desk monitor; it must remain usable at 1024 px and readable at 390 px for a quick check. Preserve all facts; do not invent payments, messaging, insurance or other features.

cases.name: Linea
cases.brief: Design a complete mobile-first prototype for Linea, the fictional public transport app of the city of Veloria, as one single-page experience. Riders use it daily, often one-handed while walking. The jobs, data and rules are settled; structure, navigation, iconography and visual direction are open. Riders must be able to: plan a trip from a saved place to a destination and compare route options; buy a ticket; show the active ticket to an inspector; keep saved places; and read service alerts. Tickets: single ride EUR 2.40, valid 90 minutes; 24-hour pass EUR 6.50; 7-day pass EUR 21. An active ticket shows its type, remaining validity counting down, a scannable code area and the rider's initials (M.K.) for inspectors. Saved places: Home (Ash Street 14), Work (Harbor Tech Park), Gym (Riverside Pool). Planning from Home to Veloria Central Library returns three options: 22 min, tram T2 then bus 41, 1 transfer, departs in 4 min, bus 41 crowding high; 27 min, metro M1 direct plus a 6-minute walk, departs in 7 min, crowding medium; 31 min, bus 12 direct, departs in 2 min, crowding low, step-free. Active alert: tram T2 delayed about 10 minutes between Market Square and Old Bridge until 18:00 because of track work. Purchase is simulated locally; buying the 7-day pass fails at payment, and the rider must be able to try again or choose another ticket without losing the selection. Primary viewport 390x844; it must also work at 820 px wide. Preserve all facts; do not invent accounts, live vehicle maps, fare capping or other features.

cases.name: Gridwise
cases.brief: Design a complete single-page monitoring workspace for Gridwise, fictional energy-monitoring software used by the facilities manager of a small university campus with six buildings. The manager checks it several times a day to spot problems and act on them. The job, data and rules are settled; structure, composition, interaction design and visual direction are open. Buildings with current load and consumption so far today: Library 182 kW, 1,940 kWh; Science Hall 311 kW, 3,420 kWh; Sports Centre 96 kW, 1,105 kWh; Student Union 74 kW, 860 kWh; Admin Block 58 kW, 610 kWh; North Residence, meter offline since 09:42, last known 140 kW. Campus contract peak limit: 950 kW. Alerts: Science Hall HVAC drawing 38% above its usual Tuesday profile since 07:15 (open); North Residence meter offline (open); Library lighting left on overnight (acknowledged yesterday by J. Park). The Sports Centre has had no alerts in the last 7 days. The manager must be able to: see campus load against the peak limit; see which buildings need attention; open one building to see its last 24 hours as hourly values (a plausible curve consistent with the figures above) and its alert history; acknowledge an open alert with a short note; and export today's readings as a CSV download generated locally. Behaviour to simulate locally: readings refresh every 10 seconds with small changes; the first load takes about 1.5 seconds; the North Residence detail cannot load readings and must say so with a way to retry. Primary viewport 1440 px; it must remain usable at 1024 px and readable at 390 px. Preserve all facts; do not invent costs, tariffs, carbon figures or equipment controls (the manager cannot switch equipment from here).

cases.name: Second Frequency
cases.brief: Design a complete single-page experience for Second Frequency, a fictional workshop restoring portable radios. Collectors and people repairing a family keepsake should understand the services and request a diagnostic inspection. The page should have a distinctive, authored character while conveying careful workmanship. The page job, offer and local request flow are settled; visual direction is open. Facts: diagnostic inspection EUR 25, credited toward an accepted repair; electronic repair from EUR 95 after approval; case and tuning restoration from EUR 65 after approval; typical inspection turnaround 5 working days; no promise that every radio can be repaired. Explain those three services, show the inspection terms and provide a request form collecting device, problem and contact email. Submit produces a local preview, explicitly not a sent booking. Include a clear way to return to editing. Preserve all facts and the EUR currency.

cases.name: Inkwell
cases.brief: Inkwell is a fictional newsletter tool. Its existing account settings page is already in site/index.html. Users report two problems: when they open the 'Digest frequency' menu it is cut off, and the 'Save changes' button jumps when an error message appears and again while saving. Fix these problems in the existing page. Keep its visual design, structure, copy and other behaviour unchanged; this is a correction, not a redesign.
